prompt: How do I create a signature in Outlook?
completion:
Below are step‑by‑step instructions for creating an email signature in **Microsoft Outlook** on the most common platforms. Pick the section that matches the Outlook client you’re using. --- ## 1️⃣ Outlook for Windows (Office 365 / Outlook 2016‑2024) | Step | Action | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **1** | Open Outlook. | No need to open an email first. | | **2** | Click **File** > **Options**. | Opens the Outlook Options dialog. | | **3** | Select **Mail** (left pane). | | | **4** | Click the **Signatures…** button. | This opens the Signature and Stationery window. | | **5** | **New** | Give your signature a name (e.g., “Work”, “Personal”). | | **6** | **Edit** the signature area: type text, paste images, use tables, change fonts, colors, etc. | • Use the toolbar to format.
• To add a picture: **Insert** → **Pictures**.
• For a hyperlink: select text → **Insert** → **Hyperlink**. | | **7** | **Choose defaults** (right side):
• *New messages*: pick your signature.
• *Replies/forwards*: pick your signature. | If you want the signature to appear automatically, check the boxes. | | **8** | **OK** → **OK** → **OK** | Close all dialogs. | **Tip:** - If you want different signatures for different accounts (e.g., work vs. personal), use the account‑specific default option above. - To remove a signature from a specific email, click **Signature** on the email ribbon and choose **(none)**. --- ## 2️⃣ Outlook for Mac (Microsoft 365, Outlook 2016‑2024) | Step | Action | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **1** | Open Outlook. | | | **2** | Click **Outlook** (menu bar) → **Preferences**. | | | **3** | Select **Signatures** (under Personal Settings). | | | **4** | Click **+** to create a new signature. | Give it a name. | | **5** | In the right pane, type/edit the signature. | Drag and drop images, use the formatting toolbar. | | **6** | In the bottom pane, choose the default signature for:
• *New messages*
• *Replies/forwards* | | | **7** | Close the window; changes are saved automatically. | | **Mac‑specific note:** - Outlook for Mac automatically inserts the default signature in new messages, but **only in the body of the email** (not in the reply chain unless you selected it). - If you want to add a signature manually, use **Insert → Signature** in the message compose window. --- ## 3️⃣ Outlook on the Web (Outlook.com / Office 365) | Step | Action | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **1** | Log into or . | | | **2** | Click the gear icon (⚙️) → **View all Outlook settings**. | | | **3** | Go to **Mail** → **Compose and reply**. | | | **4** | In the **Email signature** box, type/edit your signature. | Use the formatting toolbar, insert images (you may need to upload them). | | **5** | Check the boxes:
• *Automatically include my signature on new messages I compose*
• *Automatically include my signature on messages I forward or reply to* | | | **6** | Click **Save** at the bottom. | | **Tip:** - You can have **one signature** per mailbox in the web client. - If you need multiple signatures, consider using Outlook for Windows or a third‑party add‑in. --- ## 4️⃣ Outlook Mobile Apps (iOS & Android) | Step | Action | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **iOS** | Open the Outlook app → tap your **profile icon** → **Settings** → **Signature**. | Edit the text; images aren’t supported. | | **Android** | Open the Outlook app → tap the **menu icon** → **Settings** → **Signature**. | Same as iOS. | | **Save** the signature. | | *Mobile signatures are automatically appended to every new email you draft.* --- ## 5️⃣ Advanced Tips & Common Troubleshooting | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Signature doesn’t appear in replies** | In Outlook desktop, check the “Replies/forwards” default. In the web client, ensure the checkbox is ticked. | | **Images missing when forwarded** | Save images locally and insert them from the local file system (not from a web URL). Use the “Insert Picture” feature. | | **Signature too long or format breaks** | Avoid overly large images or complex tables. Keep the signature under 5 KB and use simple formatting. | | **Using a template with placeholders** | Create a signature in Word, copy‑paste it into Outlook. For placeholders (e.g., “[Name]”), manually replace when composing. | | **Multiple accounts with different signatures** | In Outlook desktop, set defaults per account (step 7). In Outlook web, you only have one; use a third‑party add‑in or export/import. | --- ### Quick Recap 1. **Windows** → File → Options → Mail → Signatures. 2. **Mac** → Outlook → Preferences → Signatures. 3. **Web** → Settings → Mail → Compose & reply. 4. **Mobile** → Settings → Signature. Now you’re ready to create a polished, professional signature that appears automatically in every email you send! If you have any specific questions (e.g., adding a company logo, multi‑language support, or how to integrate with a CRM), feel free to ask.
